scope: Paired low/high grip-force reward-proxy repeatability and footprint sensitivity across two production models and two declared physical radius schedules, with all choices retained.

reports.scope:
Measure raw-stress reward repeatability and paired grasp-force discrimination.

Each of eight frozen conditions is duplicated with only the commanded strong
grip force limit changed. The original approach/lift/slide/weak/release schedule,
arm targets, radii, friction and resets are retained. Intrusive observations
make this a behavioral experiment, never a throughput benchmark.
reports.limitations: Raw stress and exposure are uncalibrated reward proxies for two explicitly controlled grip choices. This is numerical repeatability and useful discrimination conditional on the chosen480-tet mesh, actual rigid contact and model/radius assumptions. It does not certify a fracture threshold, physical stress accuracy or complete RL training. Different models can change stress rankings without changing rigid motion. All values and any rejected input remain; intrusive observer timing is excluded from throughput.

limitations: Twelve paired observations per condition (three restarts times two models times two radius schedules), not twelve independent physical experiments. Stable ordering in this tested set is weaker than separation exceeding an absolute model/radius band. Neither validates continuum or experimental stress, a fracture threshold, or decisions inside unresolved uncertainty.
